title: Build for the Memo, Not the Demo — Shawn Chan, China Resources Holdings
talk_summary: A finance/investment-committee insider argues AI products are built to impress in demos but fail when output must survive adversarial scrutiny (a 'memo'), and enumerates six concrete trust failures (unranked sources, inconsistent numbers, hidden contradictions, facts blended with guesses, unverifiable citations, no accountable human) plus five plumbing fixes. The fixes are cheap, non-model changes: source trust levels, cross-checking numbers, surfacing contradictions, labeling guesses, click-through citations, and a logged human approval gate.

takeaways.technique: Surface contradictions instead of smoothing them
takeaways.what_they_do: When sources or artifacts disagree, the system raises a flag for a human rather than silently picking the nicer/fluent version; the disagreement itself is treated as the signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A contradiction is not a bug a contradiction is a gift... make sure that the argument happens in front of a human instead of quietly along inside box.

takeaways.technique: Facts vs guesses must be visibly separated
takeaways.what_they_do: Tag every claim as proven or estimated so a reader can see at a glance what is verified; the tag must survive copy-paste into other documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Facts and the guesses have to live in separate box... Label your guesses, a tag, a color, anything that survives being copy pasted into someone else's slides.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each sentence links to its exact source paragraph; the 30-second test is whether one click lands on the source, not a citation list at the end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When someone points at a sentence and says, "Show me where this come from." You either click once or land on exact source paragraph.

takeaways.technique: Logged human approval gate with audit trail
takeaways.what_they_do: Every real decision ends at a named human who signs; the system logs who reviewed what, when, and what changed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A real human approval gate and is logged. Who's Who reviewed what change when they signed. That log is audit trail.

takeaways.what_they_do: Rank sources by trust (audit filing > analyst note > group chat) and attach the trust level to each retrieved chunk instead of treating nearest text as gospel.
The system refuses to ship a document where figures don't reconcile across pages, replacing a human checking at 2am with a mechanical consistency check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The system refuse to ship a memo where the figures don't match. No human checking at 2:00 in the morning.
